about: THE CARDS OF THE EASTERN SEA (region baltic_east: Birka, Helgo, Uppsalir, Paviken, Truso, Grobin, Aldeigjuborg). Written 7 Oct 2026 by the region's weaver from the ports' places files (Data/places/<port>.json), the dossiers (Design/content/dossiers) and the spine (Design/content/spine.json). A draft in the game's own files, for the user to overwrite. Each card names its port with port.id in its 'when' and is listed in its site's 'do' in the places file; three cards are the far end of a line that begins here and lie in ports of other regions (harbour.catlas_count.dorestad, harbour.counts_amber_home.dorestad, harbour.count_stick.hleidr), so they are in no site's 'do' yet. The words are in Data/writing/baltic_east.json under baltic_east.<port>.<card>.<slot> (l_ a line, o_ an option, out_ what comes of it); a picture line for each card is there as art.<card id>. The spine's thread flags are set only for the step they name (sv_first_dirham, sv_scale, sw_buyer_known, sw_ran_blades, lf_trail_north, rd_setter_known). This file's own flags begin be_; flags the places files already name are kept as they are (tr_three_silvers, tr_purse_witness, tr_purse_home, tr_purse_taken, tr_wulfstan_asked, tr_wulfstan_told, uppsalir_stick_carried, uppsalir_stick_unread, uppsalir_stick_read, uppsalir_embers_carried, uppsalir_bought_off, uppsalir_stood_feast, uppsalir_debt_carried). Grand rewards are unlock_ flags (Design/content/CHAINS.md) and are few: these are ordinary cards, and the chains carry the large payouts. Lines that run through several ports: the brass (Helgo, Birka), the tally stick (Helgo, Birka), the bundle of beads (Birka, Uppsalir), the false word of fire (Birka, Grobin), the stone with two birds (Grobin, Paviken), the dried root (Grobin, Truso), the king's ships (Birka, Grobin, Birka again), the purse under the post (Truso, Paviken), the five sticks of Delling's door (Uppsalir, Paviken, Aldeigjuborg, and back), the count's amber (Truso, Dorestad), the widow's bag (Birka, Dorestad), the count of the lay (Uppsalir, Hleidr), the bronze man (Helgo, and wherever the house has been). Riddles said aloud are our own plain renderings of Gestumblindi's riddles (Vigfusson and Powell 1883) and of the lay of Vafthruthnir (Bellows 1923), both in texts_793.json; nothing is quoted from a modern translation. Every source is in the card's 'note'; (?) marks what was not checked; LATER marks a source written long after the thing it tells.

cards.note: Birka, the stone-footed jetties: the king's man who keeps the town says where a ship lies. From 829 to 851 he is Herigar (birka.herigar, cast.herigar: Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 11, 19, tr. Robinson 1921: 'the prefect of this town ... a counsellor of the king'); before and after him the role forge's keeper. A share of cargo to the king through the prefect is likely, not recorded (B. Magnus, Birka, 1999): here it is a gift, not a toll. The pile line off the town is real, its date not given (Magnus); the game drives it after the exiled king's ships of about 847 (Rimbert c. 19). A rumour that is true: wine is dear at Birka for sixty days (the card makes it so). Wine is the lord's drink in the north: goods_793.json rhenish_wine, wanted 3 in svealand.

The forty green beakers answer places/colonia.json (colonia.wine_factor: a Svea ordered forty through a Frisian and paid half). The tally stick is helgo.going_quiet beat 2: a plot for the weight of sixty pennies is places/birka.json birka.work.plot's yearly due, used here as his word. cards.note: Birka, the strangers' booths, in the sailing months before 853. A rumour that is NOT true: a Dane says the Cori have burnt the Gotlanders' booths at the hornbeam fort (Grobin). They have not: the place stands until the Svear burn it about 854 (Rimbert c. 30). The lie is answered at Grobin by harbour.rodlikns_bench.grobin, which sets be_grobin_lie_found. Honey 'and perhaps salt in grey Slav pots' and lime-flower pollen in the town's dung (Magnus 1999); the Wend's word of Dragomir answers the spine's cast.dragomir (reric.dragomir), who wears a cut white coin on a thong. A string of beads (12 d) for a crock of honey (24 d) is a good bargain for the Frisian: the Wend 'weighed them against nothing; he just looked' (places/birka.json, birka.bead_maker).

cards.note: Birka, the iron smith's yard, with blades aboard. The spine's thread swords_north, hook for Birka: Holmfast buys blades without hilts and sells them at Aldeigjuborg for furs and dirhams (the story birka.blades_without_hilts beats 3 and 4; sets sw_buyer_known and, since the blades have left the realm unseen, sw_ran_blades). The law: byrnies not to be sold out of the realm (Herstal 779 c. 20); no arms to merchants (803); nothing east but by the border posts, and no arms (Thionville 805 c. 7): spine.json, swords_north. The finds: about 170 blades inlaid with the Ulfberht name, most of them in the north and east (Wikipedia 'Ulfberht swords'). 180 d a blade is three times goods_793.json sword_blades (60 d, from 800); 230 d for a hilted sword against 84 d on the Rhine. No profit and a clean name is the free road.

cards.note: Birka, the open plain: a lawsuit and an oath. A townsman says before the standing men that he was paid by count and the count was light. The thing of Birka on 'an open plain' is Rimbert c. 19 and 26-27 (Robinson 1921); how a suit was heard there is not recorded: the ring of men, the lawman and the townsman who must stand beside a stranger are the game's, on the custom that a host answers for his guest (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md; places/uppsalir.json, uppsalir.holmgeir) (?). An old penny worn light is true to the time: the reform of 793-794 made the denier heavier and old coin went by weight in the north (spine.json, silver_road). A house that carries the northern scale (sv_scale) wins by it.

cards.note: Birka, the open plain, in the years without a priest (845 to 851). The spine's thread cross_and_grove, hook for Birka: 'Herigar alone at the thing, dry in the rain'; the story birka.dry_in_the_rain beat 4. Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 19 (tr. Robinson 1921): the heathens jeered at Herigar at an assembly held on an open plain; rain was at hand; he bade them call on their gods to keep it off them and he would call on his; they sat together on one side, he and one small boy on the other; the rain soaked them and blew the leaves of their shelter of branches on them, and not a drop touched him or the boy. Herigar is birka.herigar (cast.herigar); the spokesman of the old party is invented. What a stranger did is the game's.

cards.note: A feast day: midsummer at Birka, which is Saint John's (23 and 24 June, Feasts.On) to the baptised men aboard. The long house on the terrace is real (twenty paces long, built about the time the town began: Magnus 1999). That the Svear feasted at midsummer is likely and not recorded for 793 (?); the three yearly offerings are Snorri's, and so is the horn drunk 'for a good year and peace' (Hakonar saga goda, about 1230): LATER, used as a custom of the table and no more. Fire, water and a seat for a guest: Havamal 2-4 (Bellows 1923, texts_793.json). Wine is the lord's drink and a rare thing here.

cards.note: A passenger to carry. Birka, the church on the dead prefect's ground, 852 to 862: Catla (birka.catla, cast.catla), daughter of the widow Frideburg, is to carry her mother's wealth to Dorestad for the poor. Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 20 (tr. Robinson 1921): Frideburg bade her daughter give all she had to the poor, 'and because there are here but few poor' to go to Dorstadt, where 'there are there many churches, priests, and clergy, and a multitude of poor people' (the first words are quoted in her line). The spine's thread cross_and_grove; the story birka.dry_in_the_rain beat 8; the unlock birka.christian_house. Dorestad is gone after 863, so she is not taken aboard after 862. That the road was 'beset by pirates' is Rimbert c. 10, of an earlier voyage. The far end is harbour.catlas_count.dorestad.

cards.note: A funeral. Birka, the grave field east of the town: most of the dead are burnt and laid under a low mound; small flat loaves go on the pyre (64 were found); scales and weights lie in the graves; the dead were asked for counsel at the mound (Magnus 1999). In 822 the dead man is Holmfast (birka.holmfast, cast.holmfast), in 828 the skald Grimulf (birka.skald); in other years a comb-maker who is invented. The woman who speaks is the weaver Fastlog (birka.weaver), Grimulf's niece, to 835, and a woman of her lane after. No rite is described beyond what the graves show.

cards.note: Uppsalir, the guest house by the hearth-keeper's door: Gillaug (uppsalir.gillaug), to 820. She gives the riddle of the dust-like maidens, r-gest-33, for nothing to anyone who sits up with the fire (riddles_793.json: given by 'the woman who keeps the hall's hearth'; Heidreks gatur 33, Vigfusson and Powell 1883; pale embers on the hearth). cards.note: Paviken, the dragging beach: Rodiaud (paviken.rodiaud), the widow whose farm owns the shore, to 811; the woman of that farm after her. The island that sank by day until fire was brought to it is the Guta saga's: LATER, told as an old tale. Salt is wanted on Gotland (goods_793.json sea_salt). cards.note: Truso, the Dane's long house, 812 to 818: the story truso.eleven_and_five beat 1 (thread silver_road). In 814/815 or soon after a purse of eleven whole coins and five pieces was put in the ground at Truso: ten dirhams of the caliphs and one drachm of the Persian king Khosrow II, two hundred years old; nobody came back for it (the deposit dug in 1986: Medievalists.net, 28 Sept 2026). The Gotland skipper who buries it, his boatload of blades for the Vistula and the witness are invented. Sets tr_purse_witness (the places file's flag). An oath of a kind: a witness's word. The end is harbour.guests_post.truso, a lifetime on, and harbour.landing_gift.paviken.

cards.note: Truso, the wood nobody cuts, before 813: Drua (truso.drua), an old woman of the kin that can make cold. Later witnesses say the Prussians held certain woods, fields and waters so holy that none cut, tilled or fished there, and barred strangers from them (Adam of Bremen, 1070s: LATER; en.wikipedia 'Old Prussians'): here a custom, with no god, rite or priest named. A crewman of the house has cut green alder for the cooking fire. Every danger warns first and there is a road that costs only pride. The bundle of dried root is the end of a favour begun at Grobin (harbour.woman_who_is_asked.grobin: grobin.buite and truso.drua send each other dried plants by the amber boats). No card here asks how the cold is made: the chain amber_road keeps that.

If the house once poured ale at a wake (changed_ests_brew_ale, the chain amber_road), he is told that at one fort they brew. ports_793.json closes Truso in 850; the dossier and this card say it stood to about 1000 (see the report).

cards.note: Truso, the mouth of the Ilfing, 950 to 1003: Mante (truso.mante), a fisherman who takes ships through the reeds. The story truso.reeds: in the second half of the 900s the silt of the Nogat began to cut the lake off from the lagoon and the sea, and a new harbour at the Vistula's mouth took the trade; in this century or about 1000 the place burned, with a thick layer of ash and many arrowheads, and who did it is not known (en., pl. and de.wikipedia 'Truso'). A rumour that is true, in 997 to 999: Bishop Adalbert of Prague came among the Bruzi after Easter 997 and was killed some days after 22 April; Duke Boleslaw bought the body for its weight in gold (en.wikipedia 'Adalbert of Prague'); no Life names Truso, and Mante does not. The work truso.work.channel (here the flag be_truso_staked). ports_793.json closes Truso in 850 (see the report).

cards.note: A funeral custom. Truso, the burning ground by the river, in every age of the port. Wulfstan, about 890: among the Este the dead of every people must be burnt, and if a single bone is found unburnt the kin must make great amends for it (the Old English Orosius: the customs from the Old English, Sweet 1883, pp. 19-21, in our own rendering; texts_793.json wulfstan has the passage only). Graves of merchants lie along the river (en.wikipedia 'Truso'); the site's own note: nobody may lie unburnt in this ground. The women with rakes, the drowned fisherman and the asking of a stranger to witness are invented, on the custom that a witness from outside the kin is the better one (as in the story truso.eleven_and_five, where the Dane points at the stranger). What the amends were is not recorded, and is not named. The Dane is Ketil (truso.ketil) to 824 and the keeper of the long house after.

cards.note: Grobin, the black earth, before 813: Botgair (grobin.botgair), the oldest of the Gotland traders, and Kantegede (grobin.kantegede), the Curonian go-between. The spine's thread silver_road, hook for Grobin's region ('Gotlanders and Svear living among heathen Curonians'); the story grobin.weighed_twice, with its three endings: the_gotlanders_man, the_curonians_guest (the flag be_curonian_guest) and the_third_scale (the flag be_third_scale; the unlock grobin.the_third_scale: needs the spine's sv_scale). Gotlanders lived and were buried here among the Curonians (en. and de.wikipedia 'Grobina'); everything goes by weight, since no coin is struck on this coast. Among Botgair's cut silver is a half dirham from the island (sets the spine's sv_first_dirham). Amber at 20 d the sack is the source price (goods_793.json amber, made in curonia); iron tools are wanted here. The Dane at the next plank is Ketil of Truso after the chain amber_road's ending end_shut. No Curonian god, rite or word is put in a mouth.

cards.note: Grobin, Rodlikn's long house (and the field of the armed men, where the old stone stands), before 819: Rodlikn (grobin.rodlikn), a Gotland widow who keeps the house where strangers sleep. The story grobin.two_birds: a flat stone carved with two duck-like birds, of a kind otherwise made only on Gotland, 0.70 m high, was set in a grave here in the later 600s and dug out in 1987 (en.wikipedia 'Grobina'; lv.wikipedia 'Grobinas arheologiskais ansamblis'); she wants one cut for her own grave. A commission: her bag of sixty pennies' weight and a drawing on birch bark go to the carver on Gotland (harbour.carvers_slope.paviken: forty to him, twenty for the carrying), and the stone comes back over the bar. Women in the flat graves wear Gotland's own brooches. She answers the false word of fire heard at Birka (harbour.strangers_booths.birka; sets be_grobin_lie_found). Her bench is the unlock grobin.kept_bench (the flag be_grobin_bench). Ravn (cast.crew.ravn) once set her a riddle.

cards.note: Grobin, the gate of the fort, before 801: Arnvald (grobin.arnvald), the head of the few armed Svear who still sit on the hill, and Kantegede (grobin.kantegede), who speaks for the forts inland. The spine's thread swords_north; the story grobin.old_tribute, with its three endings: blades_to_the_hill (the flag be_grobin_blades_hill), blades_to_the_forts (be_grobin_blades_forts) and no_blades (be_grobin_no_blades). The Cori 'had in former time been in subjection to the Swedes, but had a long while since rebelled' (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 30, tr. Robinson 1921); one of the three grave fields is 'military in character', with men of the Malar valley under low mounds with their weapons (en. and de.wikipedia 'Grobina'). By the Latvian accounts the Curonians take the place over about 800. The Frisian who promised blades through a Dane is cast.thiadbod. Swords carried here have left the realm unseen (sets the spine's sw_ran_blades). Twenty timbers of grey squirrel, or twenty sacks of amber, for three swords is about twice their Rhine price and more: a turn payout. Every danger warns: each has a man watching the other's door.

A favour: a bundle of dried root for the woman who is asked at the lake of the Este (truso.drua), delivered by harbour.alder_spring.truso. cards.note: Grobin under the Curonians, 801 to 852: Wissegerde (grobin.wissegerde), Kantegede's son, who runs the market once the hill is theirs. By the Latvian accounts the Curonians take the settlement over about 800, and between 800 and 850 the Gotlanders and Svear stop being buried here (lv.wikipedia 'Grobina'; the pages disagree). A truce counted in days is the saga's picture of a Kurland market (Egil's saga c. 46, 13th century: LATER; no place named). What a house did in his father's time is remembered: the endings of grobin.weighed_twice and grobin.old_tribute (be_curonian_guest, be_grobin_blades_forts, be_grobin_blades_hill; the unlock grobin.gate_without_gift). Amber is thrown up by the autumn gales and is cheapest then (goods_793.json amber; seasons). The Birka man who asks too many questions is grobin.vigfast.

cards.note: Aldeigjuborg (in speech Aldeigja), the mouth of the small river and the fort at the Lyubsha mouth, before 823: Budimir (aldeigjuborg.budimir), river pilot of the fort at the stream mouth. The Lyubsha fort, Slav on an older Finnic site, silted and was given up in the later 800s (ru.wikipedia 'Lyubsha fortress'); the lake has shoals along its south shore and steep waves (Research/water_levels/baltic_east.md); the upper Volkhov can reverse its flow (en.wikipedia 'Volkhov (river)'). He is paid in things that keep: iron, salt, cloth. The marks count toward unlocks_793.json unlock_pilot_volkhov (here the flag be_volkhov_marks; the unlock aldeigjuborg.lake_marks). cards.note: Aldeigjuborg, the trading bank, before 840: Ihalempi (aldeigjuborg.fur_dealer), who speaks for the trappers, to 828; the woman at her blanket after. Finnic people lived on this river before Slav or Northman; furs are bought with beads (ru.wikipedia 'Staraya Ladoga': the bead shop of the 780s to 830s; 'a bead for a slave' is a 10th-century Arab traveller's word, LATER). Forty skins to the timber. Tribute of a squirrel skin from each hearth is the Primary Chronicle's, under 859: LATER, said as what happens on other rivers. A string of beads for a timber of squirrel and three for a timber of marten are the trappers' own prices: the best margin on this bank, once a call.

cards.note: Aldeigjuborg, the bead-maker's shop, before 840: Milava (aldeigjuborg.milava), to 830; the woman at her fire after. The shop is real: glass eye beads made by a low-heat method learned from the Arab lands, from the 780s to the end of the 830s, and its beads bought furs (ru.wikipedia 'Staraya Ladoga'; de.wikipedia 'Staraja Ladoga'). The story aldeigjuborg.bead_for_a_pelt beat 2: she will not take silver, she wants glass to melt. A sack of raw glass (20 d on the Rhine) for four strings of eye beads, which buy furs on the bank (harbour.blanket_on_the_bank.aldeigjuborg). A commission for raw glass at half again its price. Her rival she has never met is Ragnvi of Birka (birka.bead_maker).

cards.note: Aldeigjuborg, the old workshop: Audvald (aldeigjuborg.audvald), smith and bronze-caster, grandson of the Gotlander who first lit its forge, to 818; the smith of the workshop after him. The spine's thread riddle_road and silver_road ('a small hoard lies here: riddles_793.json rw_hoard_ladoga'); the story aldeigjuborg.corpse_on_a_corpse beats 1 and 4. He sets the riddle of the corpse on a corpse, r-gest-24 (riddles_793.json: given by one who winters on the Volkhov; Heidreks gatur 24, Vigfusson and Powell 1883; a dead horse on an ice floe), said here in our own words; the riddle pays its own reward, the place of the small hoard (the oldest dirham hoard of the town, youngest coin 786), and harbour.between_two_mounds.aldeigjuborg follows. The workshop and its tool hoard are real, in the oldest layer of the 750s, and the first settlers were perhaps Gotlanders (ru.wikipedia 'Staraya Ladoga'); the bronze finial with the horned head-dress, 'the singing Odin', is real: the horns are a head-dress on a figure, and nobody wore such a thing. The story aldeigjuborg.bare_blades beat 4: he fits northern hilts to bare Frankish blades. Ravn (cast.crew.ravn) sat a bench with him one winter on Gotland.

cards.note: A funeral. Aldeigjuborg, the grave-field on the far bank (Plakun), from 850 while the Northmen here are heathen: a dozen small mounds over cremations, boat rivets lying where a hull was burned, and one larger mound with a timber chamber and a horse (ru.wikipedia 'Staraya Ladoga' and 'Plakun'; dossier aldeigjuborg). Scales and weights go into Northmen's graves. The dead skipper and his partners are invented; the work aldeigjuborg.work.mound is how a house buries its own here. Nothing is said or shown of any rite beyond the burning of the boat.

cards.note: Aldeigjuborg, the fort on the point, 1019 to 1030: Ragnvald Ulfsson (aldeigjuborg.ragnvald), a jarl of the Gauts and cousin of King Olof of the Svear, who holds the town as the bride-gift of Olof's daughter Ingigerd, married to Yaroslav (Heimskringla, the saga of Olaf Haraldsson, about 1230: LATER, and told only there; en.wikipedia 'Ragnvald Ulfsson'). The story aldeigjuborg.black_stone beat 4 and the unlock aldeigjuborg.jarls_peace (here the flag be_jarls_peace). Jarl Eirik Hakonarson took and burned the fort about 997, and his skald Eyjolf praised it about 1010 (the Bandadrapa); the burnt layer was found in the 1980s. Yaroslav's law for the men of Novgorod, 1016: a man from over the sea clears himself by his oath alone (Novgorod First Chronicle; the wording not re-read (?)). In the brothers' wars hired fighting men go up the river, and a ship that carries them is well paid. The man at Uppsalir who knows English silver is uppsalir.sigvid.

cards.note: The end of Delling's door, on Gotland, from 871: with the fifth answer found on the middle mound at Uppsalir (riddle r-vafth-52 solved; harbour.dellings_door.uppsalir) the house knows that the chain points at a farm in the north-east of the island. The spine's thread riddle_road, hook for Uppsalir: the chain 'leads to silver under a floor on Gotland'. The story uppsalir.dellings_door beat 6, with its endings lifted (sets uppsalir_door_lifted, the places file's flag; the hoard by open_fetch spillings, hoards_793.json) and told_the_farmer (sets uppsalir_door_told; about 1,200 d in arm-rings), and the story paviken.dellings_door, ending told_the_farm; the third ending, kept_the_chain, is chosen before Arnfast at Uppsalir, and shuts this card. The Spillings hoard is real: about 67 kg of silver, mostly dirhams, with arm-rings, under the floor of a building on a farm in Othem parish, youngest coin 870/871, found in 1999 (riddles_793.json rw_hoard_spillings). The farmer, the bay, the skald's boy and every word are invented; the farm lies two days round the north of the island from Paviken, which is the game's Gotland port. That the Gotlanders judged thieves by their own law and no king's is the Guta law (LATER). A deed for robbing a host's ground is wanted and does not exist: the flag carries it, and harbour.landing_gift.paviken answers it.
